title: Submit Your Questions: Will Anyone Keep You Safe From AI?
gist: A short promo for a WIRED subscriber-only Backchannel livestream on Big Tech and AI safety (December 2), framing the AI-safety debate as having 'lost the plot' and arguing the industry has not made changes that reassure people. (Note: the raw URL slug refers to AirPods deals, but the text is the livestream announcement; card is extracted from the text.)

insights.claim: WIRED's Backchannel team frames the AI safety conversation as having 'lost the plot', with disagreement over which catastrophe matters most but broad expert alignment that society is in real trouble.
insights.speaker: Sandra Upson
insights.so_what: Mainstream tech media framing of AI risk as diffuse but serious supports continued regulatory pressure on AI developers.
insights.quote: The AI safety conversation, as Lauren Goode put it, has lost the plot.

insights.claim: Despite proposals such as a pause in model training and a data center moratorium, the AI industry has not made changes that put people at ease about AI safety, according to WIRED.
insights.speaker: Sandra Upson
insights.so_what: Unaddressed safety concerns keep moratorium-style regulatory proposals in play — a tail risk for data center buildouts.
insights.locator: Though a pause in training models

insights.claim: WIRED argues critical infrastructure appears increasingly vulnerable, tying AI safety to cyber risk such as rogue-agent attacks.
insights.speaker: Sandra Upson
insights.so_what: Supports the secular demand narrative for AI-era cybersecurity.
insights.quote: critical infrastructure seems more and more vulnerable every day
